title: Understanding the Lighting Facts Label: Lumens, Wattage, Kelvin, and Integrated LEDs
summary: This short educational segment explains how to read the Lighting Facts label on modern light bulbs. It emphasizes lumens as the brightness metric, clarifies that wattage represents power consumption rather than brightness, and provides practical comparisons (e.g., 800 lumens roughly equals a 60-watt incandescent). It then introduces color temperature in the Kelvin scale, noting that lower numbers feel warmer while higher numbers feel cooler, with 2700–3000 K suggested for a traditional look. The video concludes by noting the rise of integrated LED fixtures, which carry the same label and can last 20 years or longer, underscoring the value of reading and understanding the label when shopping for lighting.
topics: Lifespan of LED and integrated fixtures

sections.title: Key labeling metrics: lumens and wattage
sections.description: Defines lumens as the primary brightness metric and explains that wattage is about energy use, not brightness; provides an example that halogen incandescent uses more watts than an equivalent LED.

sections.title: Color temperature and the Kelvin scale
sections.description: Describes how lower Kelvin values yield warmer light and higher values yield cooler light, with a traditional look favored around 2700–3000 Kelvin.

sections.title: Integrated LED fixtures and labeling
sections.description: Notes the trend toward integrated LED fixtures, which still carry the Lighting Facts label and can last 20 years or longer, reinforcing the value of reading the label when shopping.
